title: Trump visits Ohio to support Husted in close Senate race
summary:
President Donald Trump was heading to Ohio on Saturday, October 3, 2026, for a campaign rally near Dayton. His visit aimed to support Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 elections, including Senator Jon Husted, who faces Democrat Sherrod Brown in a closely watched race.

Husted was appointed to the Senate after JD Vance left his seat to become vice president. Now Husted is running to win the seat in an election. Brown, who served three terms in the Senate, is trying to return after losing to Republican Bernie Moreno two years ago.

The Ohio contest matters because it could help decide which party controls the Senate. Democrats have identified Ohio as an important state for winning a majority. Senator Tim Scott, who leads the Senate Republicans’ campaign committee, said this week that the race between Husted and Brown was about even.

The economy is another major campaign issue. Trump has argued at rallies that the economy is doing better than voters believe. However, polls show that Americans are unhappy with his handling of it. People in the Dayton area are concerned about living costs, and nearly 1,400 workers recently lost their jobs at a nearby Springfield truck factory.

The candidates also disagree over data centers. These large buildings hold computers that support services such as artificial intelligence. Some voters worry about their effects on electricity prices, farmland and water supplies.

Brown has criticized Husted’s role in bringing data centers to Ohio, including tax breaks for technology companies. Scott defended Husted, saying he supports responsible development and would oppose a project if the community did not want it. Trump strongly supports data centers, arguing that they help the United States compete with China in artificial intelligence.

Ohio also has a close race for governor. Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a business owner and former presidential candidate, faces Democrat Dr. Amy Acton, the state’s former health director. Despite Ramaswamy’s large fundraising advantage, the contest remains competitive with weeks left before voting day.
why_it_matters: The Ohio Senate contest could influence which party controls the Senate. Economic concerns and disagreements over data centers are major campaign issues, while the state also has a competitive governor race.
